title: API gateway: standardized error contract for data residency policy violations (streaming + non-streaming)
creator: Amara Diallo
project: Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation: Hosted data residency enforcement
description:
Context
Hosted data residency enforcement requires deterministic blocking at request time when a request would be routed outside of the org/project/API key allowed region set. Today, different gateway paths return inconsistent errors (some 4xx JSON, some generic 500s, streaming path sometimes returns a generic upstream failure after headers are committed).

This ticket standardizes the public error contract for residency violations at the API gateway layer and ensures parity across:
- non-streaming endpoints (JSON response)
- streaming endpoints (SSE/chunked)

Goals
1) Single, documented HTTP status + machine-readable error code for residency policy violations.
2) Include request_id and policy_id (when available) in the response so customers and Support can correlate.
3) Ensure behavior is consistent across endpoints and SDKs (Python/TS) can map to a dedicated exception.

Non-goals
- Redesign of all Redwood API error payloads (scope limited to residency blocks; we follow existing envelope shape as much as possible).
- Implement policy evaluation logic itself (owned by routing/policy engine); gateway only enforces the error contract + translation.

Decision / Contract (per ADR-022)
HTTP status:
- 409 Conflict for residency policy violations ("request conflicts with configured residency policy")

Error code:
- residency_policy_violation

Response body (JSON, non-streaming):
- error: "residency_policy_violation"
- message: human readable guidance, stable-ish phrasing (see templates below)
- request_id: required (gateway-generated if missing)
- policy_id: optional (present when a specific policy object is evaluated; omit if not available)
- help_url: optional (docs link for troubleshooting)

Headers:
- x-request-id: always set
- content-type: application/json

Message templates
- Base: "Request blocked by data residency policy. Update your allowed regions or send the request to an allowed region endpoint."
- If request is explicitly targeting a disallowed region: include both "requested_region" and "allowed_regions" in message string (keep as text; we are not adding nested fields in v1).
- If policy missing/invalid configuration detected (should be rare): message points to Console settings page + Support.

Streaming behavior
Primary rule: residency should be evaluated before committing streaming headers.
- If violation is detected pre-route (expected path): return standard 409 JSON response (do not start SSE stream).
- If an upstream/downstream component returns a structured residency violation after the stream has started (should be extremely rare): gateway will emit an SSE terminal event:
  - event: error
  - data: {same fields as JSON payload serialized as a single JSON string}
  - then terminate the connection.

Implementation notes
- Gateway should translate internal errors from routing/policy engine into the standardized payload.
- Ensure both /v1/chat/completions and /v1/completions (and any legacy aliases) share the same middleware / error mapper.
- Ensure request_id is always present:
  - If incoming header x-request-id exists, validate length/charset and reuse; else generate.
- policy_id sourcing:
  - Read from residency decision context propagated from routing (e.g., decision.policy_id). If missing, omit.
- Logging:
  - Gateway logs should include request_id, error_code, policy_id (if present), and selected/requested region fields (no customer content).

Acceptance criteria
- Non-streaming endpoints return 409 + standardized JSON payload for residency blocks.
- Streaming endpoints:
  - If blocked pre-route: respond with 409 + JSON (no partial stream).
  - If blocked post-headers: emit SSE "error" event and close.
- Response always includes request_id (and x-request-id header).
- policy_id included when available and approved by Security/PM (see internal thread); otherwise omitted.
- Error payload matches ADR-022 exactly and is referenced by docs.
- Integration test coverage added/updated for:
  - pinned EU org hitting US endpoint
  - streaming request blocked (no generic 500)
  - request_id propagation

Links
- ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-022-error-contract-for-residency-violations.json
- Related: ENG-4827 (routing enforcement), PM-1490 (error messaging requirements)
- Support signal: SUP-28577 (streaming endpoint returning generic 500)

Rollout
- Behind feature flag: residency_enforcement_error_contract_v1
- Enable in staging first; run E2E suite; then progressive rollout by region.

Risks / edge cases
- If any handler begins streaming before policy evaluation, we may still leak a generic upstream error. Enforce order: auth -> policy eval -> response mode.
- Clients expecting OpenAI-style error envelope: we’re keeping existing Redwood envelope fields; update SDK mapping to present a dedicated exception with error_code/request_id/help_url.

Outcome
Implemented in PR-21533 and validated against staging repro from SUP-28577.
comments: 2025-02-07 (Amara Diallo): Creating as a P0 due to customer-facing impact. Support has at least one enterprise customer seeing generic 500s on streaming when pinning is enabled (SUP-28577).

2025-02-08 (Brian Murphy): Drafted contract to match ADR-022: use 409 + error_code residency_policy_violation. Please confirm policy_id exposure is OK from Security/PM; otherwise we’ll omit until approved.

2025-02-10 (Naomi Feldman): Confirmed 409 is acceptable and aligns with PM-1490. On policy_id: OK to include when it’s a stable internal identifier (not containing customer info). Ensure it’s optional and documented as such.

2025-02-11 (Marcus Lin): Security review: policy_id is OK if it’s an opaque UUID and does not encode region/customer metadata. Ensure logs do not include prompt or request body. Add unit test to prevent accidental inclusion of request payload in error body.

2025-02-14 (Brian Murphy): Implemented shared error mapper in gateway middleware for all completion/chat endpoints. Added behavior for streaming-after-headers: send SSE event:error + data JSON string, then close.

2025-02-17 (Sean Gallagher): Please add a counter for residency_policy_violation at gateway with tags: endpoint, region, is_streaming, has_policy_id. This will help confirm block rate and catch regressions when we turn on enforcement.

2025-02-19 (Brian Murphy): PR up: sources/github/redwood/pr-21533-gateway-return-409-for-residency-policy-violation.json. Includes request_id generation + x-request-id header, optional policy_id passthrough, and tests for streaming/non-streaming.

2025-02-21 (Amara Diallo): Tested staging with INT-9312 seeded org: streaming now returns deterministic 409 JSON (no generic 500). Marking ready once routing team confirms decision context fields are stable.
2025-02-24 (Brian Murphy): Merged PR-21533. Follow-up filed separately to unify help_url across docs + SDKs once docs PR lands (PR-1189).
